name: Laurence Housman
bio: Poet, dramatist, novelist and artist (1865-1959), younger brother of A. E. Housman. He sent Wilde his book of imaginary legends All-Fellows in August 1897, three months after Wilde came out of Reading, and five of Wilde's replies survive, running to the end of 1898. In 1923 he published Echo de Paris, a reconstructed dialogue recording Wilde's conversation in his last years, which remains one of the standard accounts of it. He was a member of the Order of Chaeronea, and when George Ives came to make his will in 1939 he left Housman a ring bearing the numbers 338 - the year of the battle at which the Theban Band was destroyed, and the number the Order took its name and its dating system from. He is on this map for two reasons: that, and the fact that he is the man Wilde told about Raphael and Fortune.
bio_note: Five letters: printed 923, 928, 1027, 1111, 1113. Dates 1865-1959 from the editors' note at printed 923.
